newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds firm, but cautious of data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds firm, but cautious of data.

text.p: Australian bonds started the week with a firm tone, but turnover was relatively light with the market showing some caution ahead of this week's key quarterly reports on inflation and wages.

The 10-year bond continued its solid rebound after its yield touched 7.75 percent last week and is now close to re-testing 7.50 percent, although a breach is likely to dependent on the outcome of the data, traders said.
Headline and underlying inflation data on Wednesday are expected to be subdued with the core rate back within the Reserve Bank's 2.0 to 3.0 percent target range.
However, the key event could prove the average weekly ordinary time earnings (AWOTE) on Thursday, particularly in light of the Reserve Bank's comments last week on its concerns over wages growth.

While those remarks, contained in the central bank's quarterly Bulletin, immediately sent yields up sharply, the market has slowly battled back and economists still give a near-even chance of an easing in policy before end-November.
The median forecast of a Reuters poll of 32 economists conducted on Friday put the probablity of an easing at 47.5 percent in that time frame.

The local firm tone of the market saw yield spreads generally tighten. The U.S. Treasury market ended Friday steady ahead of a virtual data free week, but Canadian bonds were stronger, buoyed by a firm dollar and higher than expected Canadian trade surplus.
